speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To begin our consultation regarding your generalized nonpruritic rash, high fever, and recent seizure, please tell me your age and how many days have passed since the fever started.

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Measles (Rubeola).

The history of high fever, seizure, and a generalized rash spreading from the trunk to extremities in an unvaccinated or recently vaccinated infant is highly characteristic of measles. Given the severity and the specific progression described, I will proceed with a clinical diagnosis based on these classic signs and symptoms.
